proposal.description: The LATCH_ASSERT bit is set whenever the protection latch reads back set, so an analog OVP trip is recorded as both OVP and LATCH_ASSERT (OCP/SCP)
proposal.reason: Suppose an analog OVP trips the shared latch during S_SS or S_RUN while latch_assert stays low. fault_reg should read 10000 but reads 11000, which reports an overcurrent trip that never happened.

proposal.description: OVP is inferred as a latch trip with no recorded overcurrent, as if every CPLD trip is shown by a recorded window trip, instead of a latch trip without the CPLD's latch_assert
proposal.reason: Suppose a host read clears the OVERCURRENT bit and the strikes then reach a CPLD latch trip while the converter is running. The OVP bit is set wrongly. In the other direction, an analog OVP trip in an episode that has already recorded a window trip leaves the OVP bit clear.

proposal.description: fault_time is re-latched whenever a live cause outranks every cause already recorded, so it gives the time of the highest-priority cause instead of the start of the episode
proposal.reason: Suppose a window trip opens an episode in S_RUN and an OTP or a latch trip follows it while the converter is still running. fault_time moves to the time of the later cause, where it should keep the time the episode began.
